questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Joshua to command 12 men (one from each tribe) to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Joshua to command the 12 men to take 12 stones from the middle of the Jordan, from where the priests’ feet stood, and carry them to their lodging place.

questions.q: What did Joshua say was the purpose of the 12 stones taken from the Jordan River?
questions.a: The stones would be a memorial to the people of Israel forever, because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh when it crossed.

questions.q: About how many armed warriors crossed over before Yahweh to the plains of Jericho for battle?
questions.a: About 40,000 armed warriors crossed over before Yahweh to the plains of Jericho for battle.

questions.q: What happened when the priests who carried the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh came up out of the Jordan and their feet touched dry ground?
questions.a: When the priests’ feet touched dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.

questions.q: Where did Joshua set up the 12 stones that the men had taken out of the Jordan?
questions.a: At Gilgal Joshua set up the 12 stones that came out of the Jordan.

questions.q: Why did Joshua say the people should tell their children what Yahweh had done for them at the Jordan?
questions.a: Joshua said they should tell their children so that all the peoples of the earth might know Yahweh’s hand is mighty, and so that they might fear Yahweh their God all the days.

commentary.text: The twelve stones placed in Gilgal.

Verses 1–9 The works of the Lord are so worthy of rememberance, and the heart of man is so prone to forget them, that various methods are needful to refresh our memories, for the glory of God, our advantage, and that of our children. God gave orders for preparing this memorial.

The priests with the ark did not stir till ordered to move. Let none be weary of waiting, while they have the tokens of God's presence with them, even the ark of the covenant, though it be in the depths of adversity. Notice is taken of the honour put upon Joshua. Those are feared in the best manner, and to the best purpose, who make it appear that God is with them, and that they set him before them.

It is the duty of parents to tell their children betimes of the words and works of God, that they may be trained up in the way they should go. In all the instruction parents give their children, they should teach them to fear God. Serious godliness is the best learning. Are we not called, as much as the Israelites, to praise the loving-kindness of our God? Shall we not raise a pillar to our God, who has brought us through dangers and distresses in so wonderful a way? For hitherto the Lord hath helped us, as much as he did his saints of old. How great the stupidity and ingratitude of men, who perceive not His hand, and will not acknowledge his goodness, in their frequent deliverances!
